title: A2A vs MCP vs agent-as-tool
summary: Three ways to use another agent's work: call it as an in-process function, reach it as an MCP tool, or talk to it as an A2A peer. Ownership, task shape, trust and latency decide which.
useIf: You must decide how one agent should reach a capability or another agent.
avoidIf: You want one answer for the whole system: mix the three, one per boundary.

explain.md: The A2A project draws the line by direction. **MCP is vertical**: it gives one agent tools and resources. **A2A is horizontal**: independent, often opaque agents discover each other, share tasks and exchange results. They complement each other: A2A between agents, MCP inside each agent [[r3]].

Microsoft's Agent Framework guidance is the same in practice. Use **agents as tools** when agents share a process and a team. Use **A2A** when you cross a service, team or organization boundary, and budget for the network latency, retries and versioning that come with it [[r12]]. An MCP tool call has no task lifecycle unless the Tasks extension is supported [[r20]], while A2A has tasks, contexts and artifacts built in [[r1]].

explain.title: Pick how to reach the other capability
explain.prompt: Flip the dials. The ranking and the reasons update.

options.name: In-process agent as tool
options.summary: A function wrapper around another agent in the same runtime.

options.name: MCP tool
options.summary: The callee is a tool on an MCP server.

options.name: A2A peer
options.summary: The callee is an independent agent with a card and tasks.

options.name: Plain API call
options.summary: A fixed HTTP contract wrapped as a function tool.

org.why: You cannot import code you do not own.

long.why: Long work needs your own durability and state handling.

relaxed.why: Latency is not the constraint, so it adds nothing.

same.why: Works, but a protocol is unneeded overhead.

team.why: A shared tool server serves many hosts.

org.why: Standard auth and discovery help across companies.

short.why: Tools and short calls are MCP's home ground.

long.why: Needs the Tasks extension and loses A2A's contexts and artifacts.

same.why: Protocol and hop cost with no boundary.

team.why: Independent releases and ownership are the fit.

org.why: Opaque execution and a trust boundary are the design goal.

short.why: Task machinery is heavier than the job.

long.why: Tasks, input-required turns, streaming and push are built in.

relaxed.why: The overhead disappears behind the work.

team.why: A stable contract suits cross-team reuse.

org.why: Works when the partner publishes a fixed API.

short.why: A deterministic call needs no agent.

long.why: You rebuild polling and status yourself.

explain.takeaway: Cross-boundary, long-running work points to A2A. Short, stateless capabilities point to tools, MCP or plain APIs. Same-team calls point to in-process.

explain.title: Answer with the boundary
explain.md: When asked which to use, name the ownership boundary, the task shape and the latency budget first. Short, schema-shaped capabilities are tools. Independent agents with long or conversational work are A2A peers. Same-team code stays in process.

whereToUse: Choosing how a planner agent reaches a specialist agent, a data lookup or a partner service
Reviewing an architecture where every helper was wrapped as an MCP tool or every call became A2A
Setting an organization-wide default: A2A for cross-team agents, MCP for shared tool catalogs
Interview answers about the boundary between agents and tools

use: Use A2A when the callee is an agent with its own reasoning and state, behind a team or organization boundary
Use MCP when the callee is a capability with a schema: a tool, a resource or a prompt
Use an in-process agent tool when one team ships both agents together
avoid: Avoid A2A for a deterministic lookup: the task machinery adds cost with no benefit
Avoid MCP wrappers for long, multi-turn agents unless you add the Tasks extension and accept the loss of context grouping
Avoid in-process composition across teams: release cycles and trust get entangled
flips: A tool call grows from seconds to many minutes: move from MCP tool to A2A or add the Tasks extension
A co-owned helper agent gets a second consuming team: promote it from in-process tool to an A2A service
A partner already ships an MCP server and the work is short: take the MCP server and skip A2A

pitfalls.symptom: Every user request pays an extra round trip to a helper agent in the same repo
pitfalls.cause: A2A was used where agents share a process and team
pitfalls.fix: Wrap the helper as an in-process tool and keep A2A for real boundaries [[r12]]

pitfalls.symptom: A long MCP tool call loses its result when the client disconnects
pitfalls.cause: A plain tool call has no task lifecycle, so there is nothing to poll or resume
pitfalls.fix: Use the MCP Tasks extension if the host supports it, or expose the work as an A2A task [[r20]]

scenarios.title: A stock lookup shared by many hosts
scenarios.situation: Many assistants need a deterministic stock lookup with a fixed schema. Calls take 80 ms and are stateless.
unknowns: Is the lookup also needed by non-agent systems?
scenarios.question: How do you expose it?

options.name: MCP tool
options.why: A schema-shaped capability reused by many hosts is MCP's purpose, with standard discovery and auth.
options.tradeoff: Tool definitions cost context tokens in every host.

options.name: Plain REST API with a function tool per host
options.why: Also serves non-agent callers and needs no MCP stack.
options.tradeoff: Each host writes its own tool wrapper.

options.name: A2A agent
options.why: There is no reasoning, state or long-running work to model as tasks.
options.tradeoff: Right if the lookup becomes a negotiating agent with follow-up questions.

flips.if: Lookups start to need clarifying questions
flips.then: Promote the capability to an A2A agent.

flips.if: Only one host will ever call it
flips.then: A function tool over REST is enough.

scenarios.takeaway: Deterministic and schema-shaped means tool, not peer.

scenarios.title: A compliance agent used by twelve product teams
scenarios.situation: A platform team runs a compliance-review agent. Product teams send drafts, the agent asks clarifying questions and may take 10 minutes. It releases weekly and the teams use different frameworks.
unknowns: How do teams authenticate to the agent?
Are results needed as downloadable artifacts?
scenarios.question: How do product agents reach it?

options.name: A2A peer with a published Agent Card
options.why: Independent releases, clarifying questions through input-required, artifacts for the report and framework-neutral clients.
options.tradeoff: Each team handles version negotiation, auth and retries.

options.name: MCP tool with the Tasks extension
options.why: Fits if the hosts are already MCP clients and conversations stay short.
options.tradeoff: Weaker support for multi-turn context and artifacts.

options.name: Shared library imported by each team
options.why: Every team must upgrade on the platform team's schedule and the agent's model and data access get duplicated.
options.tradeoff: Right only for pure, deterministic rules with no model or data dependency.

flips.if: The review becomes a fixed rule check under 1 second
flips.then: Expose a plain API or MCP tool.

flips.if: The data is regulated and each call needs per-user delegation
flips.then: Keep A2A but design authentication and delegation first (see A2A authentication and trust).

scenarios.takeaway: Another team's long, conversational agent is an A2A peer.

quiz.q: Match each approach to the situation it fits best.

pairs.r: One team ships both agents in one process
Short, schema-shaped capability reused by many hosts
Independent opaque agent with long-running, multi-turn work
Fixed contract with no reasoning needed

quiz.explain: Each pairing follows the boundary and task shape. In-process removes protocol cost, MCP standardizes tools, A2A models independent agents and tasks, and a plain API suits a fixed contract.

quiz.q: A vendor's analysis agent is wrapped as an MCP tool. Jobs take 12 minutes and calls fail when the client connection drops. What is the most direct fix?
options: Raise the client timeout to 15 minutes
Retry the same call three times
Switch the tool to a cheaper model
Use a protocol with a task lifecycle: the MCP Tasks extension or an A2A task
quiz.explain: The cause is that a plain tool call has no task handle to poll or resume. A longer timeout still loses the result on disconnect, blind retries repeat 12 minutes of work, and the model choice is unrelated.

flashcards.front: How does the A2A project describe the MCP and A2A split?
flashcards.back: MCP is vertical (an agent to its tools and resources). A2A is horizontal (independent agents to each other). Use A2A between agents and MCP inside each.

flashcards.front: When is an in-process agent tool the right call?
flashcards.back: When one team ships both agents in one process. A2A adds network latency, retries and versioning that only pay off across boundaries.

flashcards.front: What does a plain MCP tool call lack that an A2A task has?
flashcards.back: A task lifecycle: ids, states, progress, input-required turns and artifacts, unless the MCP Tasks extension is used.
